topics.title: 2017 MathCounts National Sprint #12
topics.text:
Zeno's tank holds 24 gallons of water.  Zeno starts filling the tank, but when it is halfway full he decides to start draining water out.  Once half of the water that he added is drained, he decides to add back half of the water that he just drained.  He then drains half of the water that he just added, and continues alternately adding or draining half of the previous quantity of water.  After 100 cycles of adding and draining water, how many gallons of water are in the tank?  Express your answer to the nearest whole number.



Ans.8 gallons




My solnThe first few terms are 12, 6,9,15/2, 33/4, 63/8, 129/16, ...  It looks like an alternating series converging to 8.



Starting with the 4th term, you can write each term as



$\left\{\frac{8\cdot2^n+(-1)^n}{2^n}\right\}$  as n goes from 1 to 97 which resolves to

$\left\{8+(-\frac{1}{2}^n)\right\}$



So the limit as n becomes large is 8, but I haven't seen limit problems in MathCounts before.  Is there another way of solving the problem?

topics.title: Logic and  Parity
topics.text:
One day a prince came to the kingdom of Logos in search of a princess's bride.

There he met a king who, hoping to ensure that his daughter married the cleverest

prince, arranged for a test. He led the prince to a hallway with 9 rooms, each

with a sign on the door. He explained to the prince that exactly one of the rooms

held the princess, and the other eight rooms were either empty or had a tiger

inside them. The sign outside the room holding the princess told the truth, the

sign outside rooms holding Tigers told lies, and the signs outside the empty rooms

could either be true or false. Here are the signs, numbered by their respective

rooms:



(1) The princess is in an odd-numbered room.

(2) This room is empty.

(3) Sign 5 is right or sign 7 is wrong.

(4) Sign 1 is wrong.

(5) Either sign 2 or sign 4 is right.

(6) Sign 3 is wrong.

(7) The lady is not in room 1.

(8) This room contains a tiger and room 9 is empty.

(9) This room contains a tiger and sign 6 is wrong.



The prince studied the signs for a while and then said, “Well that’s not fair, this

is unsolvable! Give me a solid clue: tell me if room 8 is empty or not!”

So the king told him, and the prince was able to solve the puzzle.

Where is the princess?

Let $BD$ meet $CE$ at $F$. Let $H$ is a point satisfy $HF \perp AC$ and the midpoint of $HF$ lie on $AC$. Let $K$ is a point satisfy $KF \perp BC$ and the midpoint of $KF$ lie on $BC$.

Prove that $H,D,K$ lie on a line and $DEF$ is a isosceles triangle.

topics.title: More MATHCOUNTS Problems
topics.text:
All problems come from the 2013 MATHCOUNTS Chapter Sprint Round. (Unless specified otherwise)

21. A right square pyramid has a base with a perimeter of 36 cm and a height of 12 cm. At one-third of the distance up from the base to the apex, the pyramid is cut by a plane parallel to its base. What is the volume of the top pyramid?



22. Four integers are chosen from 1 to 10, inclusive, with repetition allowed. What is the greatest possible difference between the mean and the median of the four integers? Express your answer as a common fraction.



24. A right rectangular prism has a volume of 720 cm^3. Its surface are is 484 cm^2. If all edge lengths are integers, what is the length of the longest segment that can be drawn that connects two vertices? Express your answer in simplest radical form.



25. What percent of the interval with endpoints -5 and 5 consists of real numbers x satisfying the inequality x+1>8/x-1?



28. What fraction of the first 100 triangular numbers are evenly divisible by 7? Express your answer as a common fraction.



27. Working in pairs, Alana and Bob can complete a job in 2 hours, Bob and Cody can do the job in 3 hours, and Alaa and Cody can do the same job in 4 hours. How many hours will it take for Alana, Bob and Cody working together to complete this job? Express your answer as a common fraction.



(MATHCOUNTS 2016 Chapter target round) 7. In a bag containing only blue and yellow marbles, there are exactly eleven yellow marbles. After five additional blue marbles are added to the bag, the probability of randomly drawing a blue marble from the bag then exceeds 70%. What is the least possible number of marbles in the bag originally?



I AM LOOKING FOR THE PROBLEM SOLVING PROCESS. PLEASE DO NOT SUBMIT ONLY ANSWERS. Thank you.
